claims.claim: Hubble notes that the field notes are held by the envoy, giving the document a stated chain of custody.
claims.quote: These notes are in the possession of Genly Ai

claims.claim: The Back of the Book runs to about a fifth of the pages of Always Coming Home and presents cultural lore.
claims.source: Wikipedia relaying Le Guin, Always Coming Home (1985)
claims.quote: about a fifth of the number of pages, presents cultural lore

claims.claim: The Back of the Book is described as carrying the attributions or annotations an ethnographic fieldworker would make.
claims.source: Wikipedia relaying Le Guin, Always Coming Home (1985)
claims.quote: attributions or annotations that an ethnographic fieldworker might make

claims.claim: Each attributed Kesh text carries a provenance line naming the teller, her town and the recipient.
claims.source: Le Guin, Always Coming Home (1985), item headings relayed by Wikipedia
claims.quote: As told by Little Bear Woman of Sinshan to the Editor
claims.page: section 'Summary', list of texts attributed to Little Bear Woman

claims.claim: A map inside Always Coming Home is captioned with the person who gave it to the Editor.
claims.source: Le Guin, Always Coming Home (1985), item heading relayed by Wikipedia
claims.quote: given to the Editor by Little Bear Woman of Sinshan

claims.claim: Pandora states the Kesh population as a seven-word sentence containing no number.
claims.source: Le Guin, Always Coming Home (1985), quoted by Wikipedia with a citation
claims.quote: There are not too many of them

claims.claim: A student reader observes that the field-notes chapter could have been written as straightforward declarative sentences but is not.
claims.source: Tori Koontz, comment on Michael Newbury's Science Fiction course blog, Middlebury College, 2019
claims.quote: which could just as easily be written in straight-forward, declarative sentences

claims.claim: A student reader describes the field-notes chapter as proceeding outward from the individual to the interpersonal to the social.
claims.source: Cole Easton, comment on Michael Newbury's Science Fiction course blog, Middlebury College, 2019
claims.quote: from the individual level, to the pairing level/interpersonal level, to the social

claims.claim: Kathy Weissman lists the topics of the Earthsea appendix as history, language, royal dynasties and dragons.
claims.source: Kathy Weissman, review of Tales from Earthsea, Bookreporter.com, 2001
claims.quote: covers topics such as history, language, royal dynasties, and dragons

claims.claim: Le Guin describes 'The Matter of Seggri' as a compendium of reports on the society of one world.
claims.source: Ursula K. Le Guin, Foreword to The Birthday of the World (2001)
claims.quote: is a compendium of reports on the society of a world

claims.claim: Le Guin places the Seggri documents in the archives of the Historians of Hain.
claims.source: Ursula K. Le Guin, Foreword to The Birthday of the World (2001)
claims.quote: These documents are from the archives of the Historians of Hain

claims.claim: Le Guin identifies the first voice of The Left Hand of Darkness as a Mobile of the Ekumen making a report.
claims.source: Ursula K. Le Guin, Foreword to The Birthday of the World (2001)
claims.quote: the first voice is that of a Mobile of the Ekumen
claims.page: paragraph on The Left Hand of Darkness

claims.claim: Le Guin defines the Ekumen in six words as a non-directive, information-gathering consortium of worlds.
claims.source: Ursula K. Le Guin, Foreword to The Birthday of the World (2001)
claims.quote: a non-directive, information-gathering consortium of worlds
claims.page: paragraph on the League of Worlds

claims.claim: Le Guin's Hainish historians are described as knowing that events keep happening and will happen again.
claims.source: Ursula K. Le Guin, Foreword to The Birthday of the World (2001)
claims.quote: know that it keeps happening and will happen again

claims.claim: The introduction to 'Unchosen Love' is signed with an address chain running from farmhold through village and watershed to the planet.
claims.source: Ursula K. Le Guin, 'Unchosen Love' introduction, excerpted on the author's official site
claims.quote: of Inanan Farmhold of Tag Village on the Southwest Watershed
